question: Ms. Blackwell gives an exam to two classes. The mean of the scores of the students in the morning class is \(84,\) and the afternoon class’s mean score is \(70.\) The ratio of the number of students in the morning class to the number of students in the afternoon class is \(\dfrac{3}{4}.\) What is the mean of the scores of all the students?
solution:
The class-size ratio determines how much each class contributes to the combined score total.

Let the morning class have \(3k\) students and the afternoon class have \(4k\) students, where \(k>0\). Since total score equals mean score times student count, their score totals are
\[
84(3k)=252k
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
70(4k)=280k.
\]
Together, the \(7k\) students have a total score of \(532k\). Their mean is therefore
\[
\frac{252k+280k}{3k+4k}
=\frac{532k}{7k}
=\boxed{76},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
